You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Problem:
To measure wrist size, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Locate a piece of flexible string (30 seconds)
Step 2. Cut the string to a manageable length (10 seconds)
Step 3. Check for any knots in the string (20 seconds)
Step 4. Wrap the string around the widest part of the wrist (15 seconds)
Step 5. Mark the overlap point on the string with a pen (45 seconds)
Step 6. Find a flat surface to work on (1 minute)
Step 7. Lay the string flat against a ruler (20 seconds)
Step 8. Record the final measurement in a notebook (30 seconds)
Step 9. Align the starting end of the string with the zero mark (10 seconds)
Step 10. Dust off the ruler (5 seconds)
Step 11. Double-check the millimeter markings (1 minute)
Step 12. Confirm the reading with a second look (15 seconds)
Step 13. Clean the pen tip (10 seconds)
Step 14. Cap the pen (5 seconds)
Step 15. Straighten the string (10 seconds)
Step 16. Ensure the string is not stretching (20 seconds)
Step 17. Remove any jewelry from the wrist (30 seconds)
Step 18. Wipe the wrist with a cloth (15 seconds)
Step 19. Clear the workspace of clutter (2 minutes)
Step 20. Put away the measuring tools (1 minute)
Step 21. Verify the string hasn't frayed (10 seconds)
Step 22. Inspect the mark for clarity (5 seconds)
Step 23. Sharpen a pencil for backup notes (1 minute)
Step 24. Position the ruler under a bright light (30 seconds)
Step 25. Check the string tension (5 seconds)
Step 26. Note the units of measurement on the ruler (10 seconds)
Step 27. Wash hands (45 seconds)
Step 28. Hold the string steady (20 seconds)
Step 29. Compare the string to a standard reference (2 minutes)
Step 30. Sit down in a comfortable chair (10 seconds)
Step 31. Gather all necessary supplies (3 minutes)
Step 32. Place the string on the table (5 seconds)
Step 33. Identify the exact mark on the ruler (15 seconds)
Step 34. Calibrate the digital ruler if using one (2 minutes)
Step 35. Relax the arm and hand (10 seconds)
Step 36. Ensure the string is snug but not tight (15 seconds)
Step 37. Read the number on the ruler (5 seconds)
Step 38. Lightly tape one end of the string down (30 seconds)
Step 39. Re-cap the marker (5 seconds)
Step 40. Secure the other end of the string (30 seconds)
Step 41. Adjust the lighting for better visibility (45 seconds)
Step 42. Look for the nearest half-centimeter (10 seconds)
Step 43. Clean the ruler surface (1 minute)
Step 44. Log the date of measurement (15 seconds)
Step 45. Put the scissors back in the drawer (20 seconds)
Step 46. Apply lotion to the wrist (1 minute)
Step 47. Find a magnifying glass (1 minute)
Step 48. Calculate the circumference (1 minute)
Step 49. Check the ruler for warped edges (30 seconds)
Step 50. Smooth out the string again (5 seconds)
Step 51. Determine which wrist to measure (30 seconds)
Step 52. Turn on a desk lamp (5 seconds)
Step 53. Put on reading glasses (15 seconds)
Step 54. Retrieve the scissors (20 seconds)
Step 55. Blow away any dust from the string (5 seconds)
Step 56. Close the notebook (5 seconds)
Step 57. Open the drawer for storage (5 seconds)
Step 58. Match the mark to the ruler scale (10 seconds)
Step 59. Peel off the tape (20 seconds)
Step 60. Round the measurement to the nearest unit (10 seconds)
Step 61. Finalize the data entry (30 seconds)
Step 62. Inspect the ruler for accuracy (1 minute)
Step 63. Organize the desk (5 minutes)
Step 64. Throw away the scrap string (10 seconds)
Step 65. Pick up the ruler (5 seconds)
Step 66. Hold the wrist at heart level (15 seconds)
Step 67. Prepare the workspace (4 minutes)
Step 68. Take a deep breath (5 seconds)
Step 69. Clean the scissors (1 minute)
Step 70. Untangle the string bundle (2 minutes)
